subject: Pricing roadmap for midterm capacity increase
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@orbithealth.com>

Cc: Kenji Sato <kenji.sato@orbithealth.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Midterm capacity increase — pricing and co-term options

Hi Nikhil,

Hope you’re well — we ran the latest usage projections for Q1 and it looks like we’ll need an additional pool of capacity mid-contract. We’re evaluating two paths:

- Option A: Add a dedicated uplift for the additional capacity and keep current contract term (pro-rata monthly pricing)
- Option B: Expand committed capacity now and co-term the whole account to align renewal dates (apply a tiered discount for the larger commit)

Can you share a high-level pricing roadmap and any constraints (minimum uplift size, approval thresholds, expected timeline for provisioning)? I attached our Q4 usage snapshot for context.

Also looping in Kenji from procurement — he’ll own the amendment paperwork.

Thanks,
Marta

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Midterm capacity increase — pricing and co-term options

Hi Marta — thanks for the context and the snapshot, that’s very helpful. Quick summary of options and next steps from our side:

Option A — Uplift (short-term add-on)
- Pro-rata billing for the remainder of the term (monthly invoicing)
- Standard uplift rate = list price + 10% (cover burst provisioning); eligible for up to 5% one-time uplift discount depending on uplift size
- Provisioning lead time: 3–5 business days for dedicated pool expansion

Option B — Co-term + Commit Increase
- Commit the larger capacity today; we apply tiered volume discounts (see attached draft): 5% at +20% commit, 8% at +50% commit, 12% at +100% commit
- Co-term aligns renewal to a single date; any partial period is pro-rated on new committed rate
- Provisioning lead time: same day / next day for pre-allocated capacity if contract amendment signed

Approvals and thresholds
- Up to 10% discount: SDR (Sales Director) approval — handled by me
- 10–20%: requires Lauren’s approval (revenue impact review)
- >20%: VP sales approval and finance sign-off

I’ve attached a concise draft with pricing ranges and a recommended path (we generally recommend co-term if you expect sustained growth past two quarters). Rachel is cc’d to confirm the capacity / perf implications.

If you’re comfortable, I’ll prepare a formal amendment and a DocuSign envelope so Kenji can route for signature. Quick question: do you prefer a mid-month effective date (pro-rate) or end-of-month co-term?

Best,
Nikhil

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Midterm capacity increase — pricing and co-term options

Nikhil — quick notes on negotiation posture:

- Orbit has been a strategic mid-market account with steady usage; we should prioritize retention and expansion while protecting unit economics.
- Recommend offering a 7% discount at +30% commit (sweet spot) with a 12% cap at +100% commit but only with a 12- or 24-month minimum term.
- Approvals: I’ll pre-approve up to 12% for a 12-month minimum with legal to sign an amendment template. Anything linear above that routes to finance.
- Preserve right to auto-scale headroom (burst) at list price to avoid overcommit exposure.

Also flag: if they want immediate capacity but are not ready to expand commit, push Option A with a one-time uplift discount rather than a long-term discount — keeps flexibility.

Lauren

--
Lauren Bishop
Sales Director, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Midterm capacity increase — pricing and co-term options

Adding technical context for the options so pricing maps to expected performance: 

- If Orbit increases dedicated GPUs by <=30% (Option A style uplift), we can reuse existing sharded pools and there’s minimal infra ops; latency and KV-cache impact negligible.
- For +50% or more, recommend redistributing traffic to a new pool (Option B); there’s a one-time rebalancing window (2–4 hours) that we coordinate to a maintenance window.
- Quantization/packing can reduce cost per token ~15% if they accept slightly lower FP precision on non-critical endpoints — could be an additional leeway for discounting.

I ran quick capacity calcs and attached the workbook with per-hour cost sims for +20/ +50/ +100% scenarios.

—Rachel

Attachment: capacity_calcs.xlsx (xlsx, 120KB)

Subject: Re: Midterm capacity increase — pricing and co-term options

Hi Marta / Kenji — thanks for the patience while we pulled internal approvals and validated the ops plan. Below are two actionable amendment paths; please reply with which option you prefer and we’ll issue a DocuSign amendment.

Option 1 — Short-term Uplift (fastest)
- +30% dedicated capacity; pro-rated monthly billing for remainder of term
- One-time uplift discount: 5%
- Provisioning: 3–5 business days
- Good if growth is expected to be transient or you want to preserve flexibility

Option 2 — Commit Increase + Co-term (recommended if sustained growth)
- Commit increase to cover +50% capacity, 12-month minimum term from effective date
- Applied discount: 8% (Lauren has pre-approved 8% at this threshold)
- Immediate provisioning upon signed amendment (target same-day allocation)
- Includes burst headroom at list price (auto-scale) and an option to revisit pricing at 12 months

Next steps:
1) Confirm preferred option and effective date (mid-month pro-rate vs end-of-month co-term).
2) Kenji — if Option 2, I’ll send a DocuSign amendment (link below) with the new commit schedules and finance SOW.
3) Rachel will schedule a brief maintenance window if we need to rebalance pools.

DocuSign amendment (draft): https://www.docusign.com/en/link/amendment-DEAL-78432
HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/record/DEAL-78432
